discussion_comments.comment_body: This should have an actual test replaying what happens in a React root not a mocked operations order.
Change to `Scheduler.log('Action')` and then below you can do `assertLog(['Action', 'Action'])`
Is this important? Isn't it sufficient to let the test run without throwing because props are frozen?

The throw is only the DEV symptom. A test that just checks the response resolves also passes with #37398's deferred freeze, which keeps handing the element the incomplete props; DevTools then reads the `null` placeholder. This assertion is the one that pins the actual invariant (the element stays a lazy until its props row completes) independent of the freeze; the assertions after the module resolves cover the no-throw outcome. I reworded the comment to say that.

we should capture fresh instances on every visibility assertion. also make sure we assert on the visiblity state before we switch to hidden as well.

holding onto the initial instance should only be relevant to assert on instance equality.

Let's use Jest's `spyOn` so that 'jest.restoreAllMocks' just works.

Otherwise we might accidentally leak further than intended depending on the Jest runner and environment setup.
Updated — the test now uses assertConsoleErrorDev instead of manually spying on console.error.

I'd suggest to use `toContain` with a looser check (same signal, less brittle).
    
`expect(headers.Link).toContain('referrerpolicy="no-referrer"');`
